name: Driving without a valid PUC certificate
mva_section: Section 190(2)(i), Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (sub-sections (1) and (2) substituted by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2026 (Act 8 of 2026), s.2 and Schedule, w.e.f. 15-8-2026, replacing the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019 wording, w.e.f. 1-9-2019)
description: Section 190(2) penalises any person who drives, or causes or allows to be driven, a motor vehicle in a public place that violates prescribed standards. Clause (i) covers road safety and air-pollution standards — the clause a Pollution Under Control certificate's absence or expiry is booked under; clause (ii) separately covers noise pollution. The 2019 amendment had made a first offence under clause (i) punishable with imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to ₹10,000 or both, plus a mandatory three-month licence disqualification. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2026 rewrote sub-sections (1) and (2) with effect from 15 August 2026: a first contravention of clause (i) now draws only a penalty which may extend to ₹10,000 plus the three-month disqualification — imprisonment no longer applies to a first offence. A second or subsequent contravention still carries imprisonment up to six months, or a fine up to ₹10,000, or both. Clause (ii) (noise pollution) now gets a recorded warning for a first contravention and a penalty up to ₹10,000 for a later one.
base_fine_text: First offence: a penalty which may extend to ₹10,000, plus disqualification from holding a licence for three months — no imprisonment applies to a first offence since the 15 August 2026 rewrite. Delhi's notified schedule compounds it at the ₹10,000 ceiling
repeat_fine_text: Second or subsequent offence: imprisonment up to 6 months, or a fine which may extend to ₹10,000, or both (the mandatory disqualification is written only into the first-offence limb; this repeat-offence wording is unchanged by the 2026 amendment)
licence_impact: Section 190(2) itself disqualifies the person from holding a licence for three months on the first offence. Section 206(4) separately obliges the officer to seize the driving licence of a driver believed to have committed a Section 190 offence and forward it to the licensing authority for disqualification or revocation proceedings under Section 19.

faqs.q: How much is the PUC challan actually charged at?
faqs.a: The statute sets a ceiling, not a fixed sum: since the 15 August 2026 rewrite, a first offence draws a penalty 'which may extend to ten thousand rupees'. States fix the compounding amount within that. Delhi's published schedule lists 'W/O PUCC — 115 CMVR / 190(2) MVA' at ₹10,000 for both the first and any subsequent offence, i.e. at the statutory maximum.

faqs.q: Can my licence really be suspended for an expired PUC?
faqs.a: Yes. The first-offence limb of Section 190(2) says the offender 'shall be disqualified for holding licence for a period of three months', and Section 206(4) requires the officer to seize the licence for a Section 190 offence and send it to the licensing authority for disqualification or revocation proceedings under Section 19.

faqs.q: Which rule is a PUC challan actually issued under?
faqs.a: Section 190(2) is the penal provision, but the emission standards themselves sit in the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989. Delhi's published schedule books the offence as '115 CMVR / 190(2) M.V.A', pairing Rule 115 of those rules with the Motor Vehicles Act penalty, so a PUC challan normally cites both the rule and the section.

statute_quote.text: Any person who drives or causes or allows to be driven, in any public place a motor vehicle, which violates the standards prescribed,––– (i) in relation to road safety or control of air-pollution, shall be liable for the first contravention with penalty which may extend to ten thousand rupees and he shall be disqualified for holding licence for a period of three months and for any second or subsequent offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
statute_quote.attribution: Section 190(2)(i), Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (as substituted by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2026 (Act 8 of 2026), s.2 and Schedule, w.e.f. 15-8-2026)
